title: MATH GAOKAO - 337
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Range of a Raw Data Set
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the range of a small data set by subtracting the minimum value from the maximum value.
questions.question: The data set is \(4,9,2,7,11\). What is the range?
questions.explanation:
The largest value is \(11\) and the smallest value is \(2\). The range is
\[
11-2=9.
\]
Therefore, the range is \(9\).
questions.hint: Find the maximum and minimum values first, then subtract the minimum from the maximum.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range from a frequency table by identifying the smallest and largest data values.
questions.question:
The frequency distribution of a data set is shown below.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
\text{Value} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\
\hline
\text{Frequency} & 3 & 5 & 7 & 4 & 2
\end{array}
\]
What is the range?
questions.explanation:
The smallest value in the table is \(1\), and the largest value is \(5\). The range is
\[
5-1=4.
\]
Therefore, the range is \(4\).
questions.hint: Use the smallest and largest listed values, not the frequencies.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the range of a data set that includes negative numbers.
questions.question: The data set is \(-5,2,-1,8,0\). What is the range?
questions.explanation:
The largest value is \(8\), and the smallest value is \(-5\). The range is
\[
8-(-5)=8+5=13.
\]
Therefore, the range is \(13\).
questions.hint: Subtracting a negative minimum value increases the range.

questions.concept: Missing Value for a Given Range
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value that makes the range of a data set equal to a specified number.
questions.question: The data set is \(3,7,7,8,12,x\), where \(x>12\). If the range is \(10\), what is \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(x>12\), the largest value is \(x\) and the smallest value is \(3\). The range condition gives
\[
x-3=10.
\]
Thus,
\[
x=13.
\]
questions.hint: Use the condition \(x>12\) to identify the maximum value, then apply the range formula.

questions.concept: Effect of Adding a Value on the Range
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether adding a new value changes the range of a data set.
questions.question: The data set is \(2,5,6,10\), and its range is \(8\). If the value \(4\) is added to the data set, what is the new range?
questions.explanation:
After adding \(4\), the data set is \(2,4,5,6,10\). The largest value is still \(10\), and the smallest value is still \(2\). Therefore, the new range is
\[
10-2=8.
\]
The range does not change because \(4\) lies between the original minimum and maximum.
questions.hint: Check whether the new value becomes the new minimum or maximum.

questions.learningObjective: Find the range of a data set given by a frequency table of counts.
questions.question:
The numbers of books read by students in a class are summarized below.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
\text{Books} & 12 & 15 & 18 & 20 & 25 \\
\hline
\text{Students} & 4 & 6 & 9 & 5 & 3
\end{array}
\]
What is the range?
questions.explanation:
The smallest number of books is \(12\), and the largest number of books is \(25\). The range is
\[
25-12=13.
\]
Therefore, the range is \(13\).
questions.hint: The frequencies tell how often each value occurs, but the range depends only on the smallest and largest values.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the new range after removing an extreme value from a data set.
questions.question: The data set is \(3,4,4,5,6,20\). If the value \(20\) is removed, what is the new range?
questions.explanation:
After removing \(20\), the remaining data set is \(3,4,4,5,6\). The largest value is \(6\), and the smallest value is \(3\). The new range is
\[
6-3=3.
\]
The original range \(20-3=17\) is not the new range after removal.
questions.hint: Remove the value first, then find the new maximum and minimum.

questions.concept: Parameter Condition for a Given Range
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value that satisfies a range condition with an inequality restriction.
questions.question: The data set is \(1,4,6,9,x\), where \(x<1\). If the range is \(10\), what is \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(x<1\), the smallest value is \(x\), and the largest value is \(9\). The range condition gives
\[
9-x=10.
\]
Thus,
\[
x=-1.
\]
The value \(x=1\) does not satisfy \(x<1\).
questions.hint: Use \(x<1\) to decide which value is the minimum before applying the range formula.

questions.concept: Range of a Combined Data Set
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range when two data sets with known minimum and maximum values are combined.
questions.question: Data set \(A\) has minimum \(3\) and maximum \(15\). Data set \(B\) has minimum \(10\) and maximum \(17\). If all values of \(A\) and \(B\) are combined, what is the range of the combined data set?
questions.explanation:
The combined data set has minimum \(\min(3,10)=3\) and maximum \(\max(15,17)=17\). Therefore, the range of the combined data set is
\[
17-3=14.
\]
The value \(12\) is the range of data set \(A\) alone, not the combined range.
questions.hint: Find the overall minimum and overall maximum of the two sets first.

questions.concept: Missing Value with an Inequality Condition
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value that produces a specified range under a given inequality condition.
questions.question: The data set is \(2,5,8,11,x\), where \(x>11\). If the range is \(12\), what is \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(x>11\), the largest value is \(x\), and the smallest value is \(2\). The range condition gives
\[
x-2=12.
\]
Thus,
\[
x=14.
\]
The value \(13\) would give range \(13-2=11\), not \(12\).
questions.hint: Use \(x>11\) to identify the maximum value, then set the difference between the maximum and minimum equal to the given range.
